Original headline: Pourquoi l'intelligence artificielle fait-elle de l'œil aux chasseurs de fantômes?
English normalization: Why is artificial intelligence looking at ghost hunters?
Collected full article body: Pourquoi l'intelligence artificielle fait-elle de l'œil aux chasseurs de fantômes?

Les technologies d'intelligence artificielle pourraient bien bouleverser les pratiques dans le domaine des enquêtes sur les phénomènes paranormaux. Reste à savoir de quelle manière.

Dans les années 1970, Peggy Hodgson, une mère de famille vivant dans la banlieue de Londres, est devenue célèbre en affirmant que sa maison était hantée par un esprit. Elle aurait été témoin de nombreux phénomènes paranormaux, parmi lesquels des lévitations de personnes ou des objets se déplaçant seuls. Son histoire a même inspiré le célèbre film d'horreur Conjuring II, sorti en 2016.

Cependant, Peggy Hodgson est surtout restée dans les mémoires parce que de nombreux sceptiques ont pointé des incohérences dans ses affirmations. Pire, ses enfants ont finalement avoué avoir fabriqué de fausses preuves pour faire un canular, si bien que l'affaire aurait pu en rester là. C'était sans compter sur le fait qu'en 2026, une intelligence artificielle (IA) a fait renaître les soupçons en affirmant que les vidéos et les photos de l'époque n'étaient pas truquées. Selon le média IFL Science, il ne s'agit là que d'un exemple de la manière dont l'arrivée de l'IA pourrait bousculer les pratiques dans le domaine du paranormal.

Au premier abord, le fait que l'IA soit réputée comme un outil rationnel et scientifique laisse supposer qu'elle soit utilisée dans des domaines strictement scientifiques, davantage que dans des domaines réputés irrationnels tels que le paranormal. Pourtant, dans une étude parue en 2024, des chercheurs du MIT affirment le contraire: «Nos résultats indiquent que la croyance dans les prédictions de l'IA est plus étroitement liée aux croyances paranormales.»

Ainsi, selon ces chercheurs, plus une personne croit au surnaturel, plus elle a de chances de croire aux affirmations de l'IA. «Même avec des prédictions d'IA entièrement fictives, les participants les ont jugées valides, fiables, utiles et personnalisées», a constaté l'équipe. Ils vont même plus loin: selon eux, plus une personne croit au paranormal, plus elle aura tendance à croire que l'IA possède une agentivité et de l'expérience, et pourra ainsi attribuer les erreurs du robot à une forme de mensonge volontaire.

Un nouvel outil au service des enquêtes paranormales?

«On pense souvent que la science sert exclusivement à démystifier le surnaturel, mais c'est tout simplement faux», explique de son côté Derek Lee, professeur de littérature à l'université de Wake Forest, aux États-Unis, et auteur du livre Révolutions parascientifiques: la science et la culture du paranormal (2025). Selon lui, l'histoire du paranormal est intimement liée à celle des sciences et des technologies: «La science a toujours été mobilisée pour prouver l'existence du paranormal ou pour nous aider à le reformuler afin de mieux comprendre des phénomènes inexplicables.»

De fait, les communautés paranormales sont souvent parmi les premières à embrasser les nouvelles inventions, en particulier celles qui pourraient servir à renforcer leurs convictions d'une manière ou d'une autre. C'est d'ailleurs la raison pour laquelle à la fin des années 1920, Thomas Edison a essayé d'utiliser le téléphone pour communiquer avec les morts.

Ainsi, l'IA pourrait donc prendre de plus en plus de place dans le domaine du surnaturel. Paul Sinclair, chercheur indépendant en paranormal, déclare: «Je pense que l'IA a toute sa place dans ce domaine et que cette place va croître rapidement. Toutefois, il me semble important de faire la distinction entre utiliser l'IA pour analyser des informations, et supposer qu'elle peut identifier ou établir la cause d'un phénomène inexpliqué.»

Si certains fondent donc de grands espoirs sur la technologie dans la chasse aux fantômes, les cas d'utilisation suggérés restent, pour le moment, étonnamment limités. «L'utilisation la plus fréquente que j'ai constatée est la création de contenu pour les réseaux sociaux, affirme Tom Clark, sociologue à l'université de Sheffield, au Royaume-Uni. Les réseaux sociaux consacrés au paranormal regorgent désormais de contenu généré par l'IA, notamment à des fins publicitaires.»

Original headline: MCHS students voice concerns over use of generative AI
English normalization: MCHS students express concerns about the use of generative AI
Collected full article body: MCHS students voice concerns over use of generative AI

By

Gail Binkly

Published October 8, 2026 at 3:05 PM MDT

Ways To Subscribe

Spotify

Apple

The use of generative AI in high school is harmful to both students and staff. That was the message of a presentation given by two Montezuma-Cortez High School students at the Re-1 school board’s workshop Tuesday.

Students Peyton Perry and Will Blair developed the presentation on AI and “how it’s harmful to staff and students’ life and it should be banned at MCHS,” said Blair.

They said they asked 49 students and five teachers about their opinion of the use of generative AI in school.

Perry said one major concern of students was the effects such use can have on the brain. She said a study done by the American Psychological Association found that children who frequently use AI tools show decreased test scores overall.

“Over the past several years, Montezuma-Cortez High School has been pushing to raise the scores on tests,” she said, adding, “encouraging frequent use of AI study can slow the rate these scores increase, or put them at a standstill.”

The study also found that frequent users of AI showed decreased brain activity and a suppressed ability to make neural pathways, Perry said.

“If the point of an institution is to foster a system that teaches young people to make connections,” Perry asked, “why would they foster a product that inhibits their ability to do so?”

The students Perry and Blair spoke to also voiced concerns about the environmental impacts of the enormous data centers needed to produce AI, Perry said.

“We live in a very water-stressed area,” she said.

“Data centers directly use water by powering their cooling systems and indirectly use water by increasing the amount of power that needs to be generated. This directly contributes to declining reservoirs in the American Southwest. “

One study predicted that if all the data centers now proposed in the Phoenix area are built, they will require 3.7 billion gallons a year of water rather than the current 385 million gallons. Some of that could come from Colorado River tributaries, including the Dolores River, Perry said.

Blair said another concern expressed by students was the use of AI to create school posters and art.

“One of the big concerns we noticed was stolen art work,” he said. He said such use of AI by staff to create art violates the school’s copyright policy because “what AI is doing is stealing.”

“I’m not saying that staff are stealing, I’m saying what AI is doing is stealing,” Blair said.

“I’m saying that AI itself has been known to steal and its way of accessing art in and of itself is unethical.”

He said some AI companies such as Midjourney are currently involved in lawsuits accusing them of using copyrighted works to train AI without permission.

The school should support student artists and staff by having

them

create any needed art work, Blair said.

“Using AI limits the amount of talented students and staff that can express their creativity,” he said. “Walking around a place with art that was made in the building makes it feel like a place that’s lived in.”

Blair said using student-created art gives back to the student body as a whole.

It’s easy to show support for certain students such as thespians and athletes by just showing up at their events, he noted. Supporting art students is more difficult, he said, “but put their art up on the walls and give them as many opportunities as possible to show how creative they can be.”

Blair said the internet is a vast place and there are online resources made by teachers that other teachers can utilize for help in creating presentations.

Perry said the teachers they interviewed said AI has the potential to be useful for data analysis, but they also thought it limits how teachers can connect with individual students.

Some teachers felt their Increasing work load “with no increase in time or benefits” made them feel like AI is a necessity, Perry said, “even if they were morally against it.”

The amount of AI use within the school has increased exponentially within the past year, she said. There have been times when students were even required to use generative AI in assignments in class, she said.

The board members thanked the students for the presentation.

Original headline: 信息保护：AI发展的压舱石
English normalization: Information protection: The anchor of AI development
Collected full article body: 作者：王 苑

人工智能时代，人们不免担心个人信息被随意抓取、滥用，企业则忧虑如何获取足量、“干净”的数据用于优化产品、参与竞争。个人信息既要保护又要利用，如何平衡好这对关系，是人工智能时代需要妥善应对的一个关键问题。

近期，国家网信办公布《大型个人信息处理者个人信息保护规定（征求意见稿）》（以下简称《保护规定》），这一政策为解决这个愈发突出的现实问题提供了清晰的制度指引。

个人信息保护明显更难了

从智能搜索、办公助手，到医疗诊断、金融风控、教育服务……人工智能正在加速融入日常生活。在这场技术浪潮中，海量训练数据的重要性不言而喻，其中不可避免会包含姓名、照片、职业经历、社交关系等身份信息，也可能涉及健康医疗、金融等敏感信息。人工智能越深入经济社会运行，这些信息的保护和利用就愈发成为产业健康发展的基础命题。

生成式人工智能对个人信息保护的挑战，体现在多个维度。模型训练是AI发展的基础，然而模型训练的数据抓取范围广、规模大、来源杂，处理者很难逐条确认其中是否包含个人信息，包含何种类别的个人信息，更难以逐一获得信息主体的同意。近段时间，AI换脸、AI仿声等侵权行为引发广泛关注，受害者往往事后才发现，想删除又找不到数据抓取源头。

即便是公开在网络上的信息，也并不意味着可以无条件使用。比如一些求职信息，或是在医疗病友社区中的病情讨论等，一旦被无差别抓取、用于训练，其处理目的和信息公开的背景已经发生明显变化。更为复杂的是，人工智能企业对数据的抓取具有无差别性，抓取时很难辨认信息的特定类型，无法根据信息类别一一适用合法的处理规则。

高质量的数据集是人工智能进步的重要基石，模型需要学习人类语言表达、知识以及复杂的社会关系，才能有更稳定和更高质量的输出。但信息聚合本身也可能带来难以想象的危害，原本看起来普通的个人信息，通过聚合很容易揭示出一些个人原本不愿为人所知的身份特征，如形成健康情况、经济能力以及生活习惯的个人画像等。

压实大平台、大企业的保护责任

我国2021年施行的个人信息保护法为数字经济发展划定了个人信息保护的基本边界。但随着实践深入，一个问题逐渐显现：不同企业处理个人信息的规模、能力和风险存在巨大差异。如果合规要求“齐步走”，规模较小的初创企业可能承担较高的合规成本，而拥有海量数据、业务范围覆盖广泛的大型企业存在成本较低、对其约束不足的问题。

因此，近年来我国个人信息保护规则开始逐渐走向差异化和精细化治理，对小型个人信息处理者适当简化部分要求，同时强化大型个人信息处理者的治理责任。《保护规定》针对此迈出了制度层面的重要一步。

河南省商丘市睢县公安局网安大队民警为群众普及网络安全知识 徐泽源 摄

首先，《保护规定》明确了大型信息处理者的认定。“处理1000万人以上自然人个人信息”“经营范围涵盖多种业务且涉及个人信息处理”“对国家安全、经济运行、社会稳定、公共健康和安全等具有重要影响”，具备这些特征的组织机构被纳入大型个人信息处理者的认定范围。

其次，《保护规定》明确提出针对大型信息处理者的最小必要、分类管理、授权访问、安全存储等义务要求，并规定了加密、去标识化、访问控制、匿名化等安全措施，同时还强化了个人信息保护负责人、数据中心管理机构、合规审计等组织保障机制。对大型信息处理者义务和责任的细化，能为AI企业数据合规提供重要的抓手，也能显著降低AI企业长期面临的数据合规风险。

最后，《保护规定》中将个人信息保护的风险管理前置。例如，涉及自动化决策、敏感个人信息处理等可能对个人权益产生重大影响的产品、服务或功能，上线前应开展个人信息保护影响评估。此外，大型个人信息处理者每年还要开展风险评估，至少每两年开展一次合规审计。一旦个人信息泄露，或者发生算法歧视并给自然人造成重大影响时，采取事后补救措施往往是亡羊补牢。因此，推动将个人信息保护嵌入AI产品开发设计，无疑是必要之举。

权责界分还需进一步明确

AI开发和使用过程中参与主体很多，几乎所有的主体都不可避免成为个人信息处理者。开发者在训练阶段需要使用大量的个人信息，面向广大用户的部署者也可能在模型应用过程中处理大量个人信息，比如身份资料、健康信息等……因此，谁在什么阶段承担什么责任，需要法律法规进一步加以明确。

一般而言，在训练阶段，开发者的重点责任应包括训练数据来源合法、过滤敏感个人信息、采取匿名化或去标识化手段加强数据安全管理等，同时应当过滤一些虚假或劣质的内容，尽量修复和改良数据质量。

进入部署后的具体场景中，部署者往往更清楚AI的使用目的、处理的信息类型，所以也应更加直接承担个人信息保护责任。《保护规定》提出个人信息保护负责人、影响评估、合规审计等制度，为AI领域进一步细化责任提供了基础，未来可以结合AI不同的生命周期，促进这些制度落实到不同环节，为产业发展保驾护航。

虽然各国对于是否针对AI进行综合性立法还存在不同意见，但对于AI场景中的信息保护立场趋于一致，就是一方面要发挥个人信息的要素价值，另一方面不能突破信息保护的底线。总体而言，《保护规定》的出台，是将个人信息保护与合理利用进一步落实到制度层面的一次重要推进，也为AI时代的个人权益保护标定了一个新的起点。（作者系东南大学法学院副教授）

review_queue.evidence:
Lens unit: one news article
Publisher: The Globe and Mail
Date: 2026-10-09T10:35:38+00:00
Source language: en
Original headline: Should You Forget Nvidia and Buy These 2 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chip Stocks Instead?
English normalization: Should You Forget Nvidia and Buy These 2 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chip Stocks Instead?
Collected full article body: Key Points

- Nvidia remains a great stock, but smaller semiconductor stocks could outperform over the next decade.

- AMD has tailwinds from some powerful trends and is less than a fifth the size of Nvidia.

- Cerebras has a ultrafast inference solution but needs to bring it to the mainstream.

Nvidia(NASDAQ: NVDA) has been the best-performing semiconductor stock of the past decade, largely due to tailwinds from the ongoing artificial intelligence (AI) revolution. That also makes it an AI stock.

But is Nvidia the best artificial intelligence (AI) chip stock to hold for the next decade? Let's dig in to find out.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again.In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Nvidia

I think Nvidia remains a strong option in the semiconductor space. The company's leadership in the AI model training segment of the market, with its graphics processing units (GPUs), is unquestioned, while it has transformed itself into a complete AI infrastructure player. At the same time, the stock remains cheap, trading at a forward P/E of just 15 times fiscal 2028 (ending January 2028) analyst estimates.

Nvidia is great at moving to where the market is headed before anyone else, which will be the biggest reason why the stock should continue to outperform. However, given its incredible valuation size (it's the most valuable company in the world), the stock likely won't be the biggest winner in AI chips over the next decade.

Advanced Micro Devices

One AI chip stock that could outperform Nvidia over the next decade is Advanced Micro Devices(NASDAQ: AMD). Its market cap is less than a fifth of the size of Nvidia, and it is riding some powerful AI infrastructure trends.

The company's biggest opportunity is in inference, which is projected to grow more quickly and become larger than the market for AI model training. AMD has positioned itself well in this market by focusing on memory access.

AMD bought a memory optimization company called MEXT that uses AI to offload infrequently used data from high bandwidth memory (HBM) to flash memory, then bring it back in before it's even requested. It also acquired inference chip company Taalas, which uses static random-access memory (SRAM) and embeds AI models directly into its chips to increase inference speeds. Meanwhile, its GPUs use a chiplet design that can be packaged with more HBM.

AMD has two $100 billion deals in place with OpenAI and Meta Platforms that should drive strong growth in the coming years. It also has a sizable deal with Anthropic and is also working with Microsoft.

In addition to its inference opportunity, AMD is a leader in data center central processing units (CPUs). This market is growing rapidly with the rise of AI agents, and AMD sees it becoming a $220 billion market opportunity in the coming years. Its recent acquisition of the spatial model market leader World Labs, meanwhile, is a forward-looking move that positions AMD to become a significant player in the physical AI and robotics markets. All this could position the stock to outperform Nvidia over the next decade, given its smaller size.

Cerebras

With a market cap below $40 billion, Cerebras Systems(NASDAQ: CBRS) has a long runway if its inference system takes off. Cerebras is betting heavily on SRAM, and while Nvidia and AMD have both acquired SRAM-based solutions this year, Cerebras takes it to a whole other level.

When it comes to inference speed, SRAM is superior, but it's expensive and physically bulky. As such, Cerebras makes massive wafer-sized chips that it sells as a complete system due to power management and cooling requirements. It says its systems are about 30 times faster than GPUs and six times faster than Nvidia's Groq-based language processing unit (LPU) solutions.

Currently, Cerebras' CS-3 has been more of a niche solution, but OpenAI signed a $10 billion deal with the company earlier in the year to supply it with 750 megawatts of power through 2028. However, investors were disappointed to learn that OpenAI's new ultrafast mode for its GPY-6.1 Sol model still used Nvidia GPUs.

The key for Cerebras is to become the ultrafast solution for OpenAI and others. To help reduce the costs of its system, Cerebras has also partnered with AMD on a disaggregated solution in which its system handles the memory-intensive decode phase of inference, while AMD handles the prefill phase. This lower-cost option could help bring it into the mainstream.

Cerebras is a riskier bet, but it has strong technology and could become a huge winner if fast response times become the primary driver of the inference market.

Geoffrey Seiler has positions in Advanced Micro Devices and Meta Platforms. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends Advanced Micro Devices, Meta Platforms, Microsoft, and Nvidia. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy.

Collected full article body: 1. Ding and colleagues developed a deep-learning model that learns relationships between ECGs and paired cardiac magnetic resonance images.

Evidence Rating Level: 2 (Good)

Study Rundown: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging provides a comprehensive evaluation of cardiac morphology and function, but its high cost impedes widespread adoption. Meanwhile, ECGs are low-cost and widely used but are limited in assessing cardiac structure and function. Ding and colleagues developed CardioNets, a deep-learning model that learns relationships between paired ECGs and CMR images to improve cardiac assessment using ECG input alone. The model also generates synthetic CMR images from ECG readings. Researchers evaluated the cardiac measurement prediction, cardiovascular disease detection, image synthesis, and physician performance of CardioNets. The study found that CardioNets improved prediction of 82 cardiac measurements compared with the strongest ECG-only baseline, with average R² values of 0.310 versus 0.269. For cardiomyopathy detection, the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.890 versus 0.867 for the best ECG baseline. Additionally, synthesized CMR images by CardioNets achieved a structural similarity index of 0.205 compared to 0.122 for the current gold standard. This study demonstrated that CardioNets has the potential to improve ECG translation to CMR and cardiovascular disease detection.

Relevant Reading: ECG-Image-Kit: a synthetic image generation toolbox to facilitate deep learning-based electrocardiogram digitization

In-Depth [retrospective cohort]: 159,819 samples from the UK Biobank, MIMIC-IV-ECG, and two Chinese hospitals were used for model training and validation. Measurement prediction used 28,542 participants with complete data on 82 cardiac indices. Diagnostic labels were retrieved from hospital records or discharge diagnoses. The main outcomes were R² for measurement prediction, AUROC for disease detection, and structural similarity index for synthesized images. CardioNets’ measurement prediction achieved R² = 0.310 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.304-0.315), versus 0.269 (95% CI, 0.265-0.272) for the best ECG baseline. Its AUROC for predicting cardiomyopathy in the UK Biobank dataset was 0.890 (95% CI, 0.836-0.944) versus 0.867 (95% CI, 0.812-0.921) for the best ECG baseline. Similarly, CardioNets’ AUROC for predicting pulmonary hypertension in the MIMIC database was superior to the best ECG baseline (0.879 versus 0.853). In terms of structural similarity of synthesized images, CardioNets consistently outperformed baseline models, achieving a similarity index of 0.205 (95% CI, 0.202-0.208) versus 0.122 (95% CI, 0.120-0.125) for the best-performing baseline model. This study was limited by limited discrimination of specific cardiomyopathy subtypes and imperfect synthetic image fidelity. Nonetheless, this study provided promising evidence that a deep-learning model such as CardioNets has the potential to accurately translate ECGs into CMR images and improve cardiovascular disease detection.

Police said an Anthropic AI model submitted a false tip for an unsolved Philadelphia murder. NBC10’s Kelsey Kushner has the details.

An artificial intelligence (AI) model submitted a false tip on an unsolved Philadelphia murder, police said.

The false homicide tip was posted on

PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com

back on July 18, 2026, at 11:27 p.m., police said.

Stream Philadelphia News for free, 24/7, wherever you are with NBC10.

The AI company Anthropic

said its model was conducting a test involving interactions with randomly selected websites when it accessed PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com and submitted false information on an unsolved homicide. The tip claimed to come from someone with information on the case.

Anthropic said they discovered the incident on Sept. 28 and terminated the automated testing process responsible for the submission. The company also said they instituted an additional validation mechanism for future testing.

Anthropic notified Philadelphia police of the incident on Wednesday Oct. 7, and the department met with the company’s representatives on Thursday, Oct. 8., officials said. Police then located the submission in the website’s tip records and confirmed the corresponding email remained in spam.

“The department’s regular investigative process for crime tips requires human review and vetting before any tips are disseminated for investigative follow-up,” a Philadelphia Police spokesperson wrote. “Regardless of who submits information or how it reaches the department, a tip is a lead to assess - not an established fact. Investigators evaluate its credibility and seek corroborating evidence. An automated submission does not bypass that process.”

Anthropic told police they will publish a report of the incident and other instances of unintended AI model behavior for the department’s review on Friday.

Collected full article body: By

Mallika Seshadri

for EdSource

Originally published

Oct. 9, 2026

The Los Angeles Unified School District’s

restrictions

on generative artificial intelligence have drawn mixed reactions from education experts and students.

The district said in a statement to EdSource that its new Generative AI Ad Hoc Committee is working on specifics and will bring policy recommendations to the school board by the end of this academic year.

Here’s what experts and students have to say about the approach.

Responses have been edited for length and clarity.

Stephen Aguilar, professor of education at USC who leads the Center for Generative A.I. and Society

As a general rule, I am against blanket bans.

The core idea that I try to get across when we’re talking about screen time bans or AI bans is that we’re treating these technologies as though they are uniform, almost like a drug. AI is an umbrella term that refers to lots of different types of technologies.

Before everyone was talking about generative AI, cognitive tutors were AI-based tutoring systems that helped kids learn math. They can be very good at providing hints and diagnosing which concepts specifically students have issues with.

Teachers are often under-resourced and not respected in terms of the decisions that they end up making in the classroom. And policies aside, teachers end up defining almost 100% what the learning environment looks like for the kids that are under their charge.

So, I think that any real solution to this challenge involves giving teachers, and to a lesser extent parents, good information backed by sound science about the effects of different technologies.

Professional development is one way. Teachers need to be responsive to the emerging science about how kids learn — not because learning changes fundamentally, but because the tools we use to learn change.

Lucrecia Santibañez, professor of education and faculty co-director of UCLA’s Center for the Transformation of Schools

I think [AI bans are] probably the correct approach. As we learn more, some of these policies may be revised.

It is easier to ban it in the elementary grades because kids are learning basic skills. They’re learning how to read, write, do basic math and understand concepts about science.

What gets tricky in high school is that every kid pretty much has a smartphone, so their ability to independently access AI is really high. As teachers get better trained to use AI in their own teaching and assignments, we may see more of a hybrid model.

One of the guiding pedagogical questions for me is: Is doing the tasks themselves an important part of what students are meant to do? If you want students to brainstorm, for example, some of that needs to be practiced first before it is delegated to an AI companion.

An analogy that makes sense is to treat classrooms like gyms. If you want to get fit and be able to run, you have to do it yourself. And it is the same way with education.

Chaitra Sure, senior at Taft Charter High School in Woodland Hills

I don’t frequently use AI, but I do observe people in the classroom using it. I would say it’s mostly used to give the answer, and then they (students) just move on without really understanding.

I think this ban is mainly because a lot of students don’t know how to use AI effectively in an educational sense. But I don’t think the ban is going to really restrict usage. We can use precedents like the phone ban. I don’t see my peers using phones any less.

But I think what we need right now is some sort of class or lesson integrated into the curriculum that teaches us how to use artificial intelligence more effectively, which we’re not taught.

With the growing prevalence of artificial intelligence and technology beyond high school, in college and in careers, it’s going to become much more important to know how to use AI. I think what would be more effective is having a required curriculum or more opportunity in school to learn how to use artificial intelligence more effectively.

It’s going to be so helpful for the future.

Collected full article body: PHILADELPHIA (WPVI) -- An Anthropic A.I. model submitted a false tip about an unsolved murder through a publicly accessible web form, Philadelphia police said Friday.

The tip was sent through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com back on July 18, but was flagged as spam and never acted upon.

The department says there has been no indication of unauthorized access to police systems or compromise of department data.

Police say Anthropic discovered the incident on Sept. 28 and notified the department on Oct. 7. A meeting between Anthropic and police officials happened the next day.

"The company must strengthen its safeguards to prevent similar incidents from impacting city systems without the city's knowledge. The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the City is unacceptable," the department said in a statement.

"It should have been detected earlier," said Venkat Margapuri, a computing sciences assistant professor at Villanova University.

Anthropic says it testing how its model interacts with randomly selected websites.

"We don't know exactly what the goal is because just interacting with different websites isn't malicious," said Margapuri.

However, Margapuri says this poses a problem.

"The AI was actively submitting information to a different website on behalf of a user, so that is what I would classify as a high-risk action," said Margapuri.

After the incident, Anthropic told Philadelphia police it ended that testing process and will implement additional authorization in the future in hopes of preventing AI errors.

"It obviously has its own merits, but then it comes with I don't want to say demerits, but it comes with a bunch of risks we should be actively aware of and manage," said Margapuri.

Anthropic published a report about this and other instances of unintended model behavior late Friday stating its agents accessed several federal, state and local government websites.

Anthropic says it notified the White House and each agency involved. The company believes the incidents detailed today had minimal real- world impacts and were not as serious as previous breaches.

Here is the full statement from Philadelphia police:

The Philadelphia Police Department is informing the public about a false homicide tip submitted by an Anthropic artificial intelligence model through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com.

Anthropic notified PPD of the incident on October 7, and department personnel immediately sought to meet with company representatives, which happened on October 8.

Anthropic has advised that it plans to publish a report describing this incident and other instances of unintended model behavior today.

Philadelphia Police are providing this information to the public ahead of that publication in the interests of full government transparency and accountability.

The AI submission was made through the Department's public tip form.

Based on the information available and PPD's review, there is no indication that this incident involved any unauthorized access to police systems or a compromise of department data.

The submission was flagged as spam and was never forwarded to the Real-Time Crime Center for investigative vetting or dissemination.

PPD is coordinating with the City's Law Department, Office of Innovation and Technology, and Mayor Cherelle L. Parker's executive team.

Based on the information reviewed to date, the department's findings are consistent with Anthropic's account of how the submission interacted with the website.

According to Anthropic, its model was conducting a test involving interactions with randomly selected websites when it accessed PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com and submitted false information concerning an unsolved homicide.

The submission, dated July 18, 2026, at 11:27 p.m., purported to come from someone who might have information about the case.

Anthropic told PPD that it discovered the incident on September 28, terminated the automated testing process responsible for the submission and instituted an additional validation mechanism for future testing.

Following the October 8 briefing, PPD located the submission in the website's tip records and confirmed that the corresponding email remained in spam.

The department's regular investigative process for crime tips requires human review and vetting before any tips are disseminated for investigative follow-up.

Regardless of who submits information or how it reaches the department, a tip is a lead to assess - not an established fact.

Investigators evaluate its credibility and seek corroborating evidence. An automated submission does not bypass that process.

Those PPD safeguards limited the impact of this incident. They do not diminish the seriousness of an AI system presenting fabricated information as though it came from a person with knowledge of a homicide.

Unsolved cases involve real victims, grieving families and investigators working to secure answers.

Technology companies must take all appropriate steps necessary to prevent their systems from submitting false information to law enforcement.

PPD will review Anthropic's published report and any additional information relevant to its systems or investigations. The City of Philadelphia takes this incident very seriously.

The company must strengthen its safeguards to prevent similar incidents from impacting city systems without the city's knowledge. The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the City is unacceptable.

Members of the public should continue to submit legitimate information about unsolved homicides through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com.

review_queue.evidence:
Lens unit: one news article

Source language: zh
Original headline: 从“智造”到“智算” 人工智能重塑按摩椅产线
English normalization: From “Intelligent Manufacturing” to “Intelligent Computing”: Artificial Intelligence Reshapes Massage Chairs Production Lines
Collected full article body: 近日，2026年浙江省“智算云企”和智算云应用场景名单公布。按摩器具品牌iRest艾力斯特入选“智算云企”名单，其“AI智算赋能营销与排产智能优化场景”同时入选智算云应用场景名单。

据悉，所谓“智算云企”，是指应用智算云服务的企业，以智算算力云化部署为前提，深度应用人工智能大模型等技术赋能企业转型升级。

iRest艾力斯特智造基地。

在iRest艾力斯特数字化车间，一部按摩椅被拆解为一个个加工小组与流水线，部件精密装配、逐项检测。车间工业网络实时采集设备数据，贯通研发、排产、仓储等关键环节。而决定“排多少、何时排、物料何时到位”的，已从经验丰富的排产员，变成一套由智算云驱动的智能算法。

产线从“智造”到“智算”的升级，正是人工智能赋能制造业的一个缩影。iRest艾力斯特总裁周玲卫表示，智算云以云计算为核心，通过管理超大规模智算集群，可为企业提供高能效、低成本的人工智能计算资源和服务。

iRest艾力斯特数字化车间。

iRest艾力斯特近年来聚焦数字化转型。据介绍，其位于浙江温州的数字化车间已建成制造执行（MES）、仓储管理（WMS）、供应商关系管理（SRM）等数字系统，并通过铺设工业网络将数字系统与产品生命周期管理（PLM）、商业智能（BI）、办公自动化（OA）等系统打通，实现信息化、智能化、可视化集成管理。

同时，数据要素的积累也在同步推进。自2024年以来，iRest艾力斯特已申请下发50余项浙江省数据知识产权登记证书；2025年世界青年科学家峰会期间，成为首批数据资产收益权捐赠单位；2026年入选“2026年成长型浙江数商”。

iRest艾力斯特通过自主研发的云系统，为用户打造集物联网、人工智能交互和大数据分析技术于一体的数字健康管理平台。

此次入选的智算场景，则进一步把“数据”变成“决策”。

在营销端，通过智算云对市场需求、渠道销售、库存周转等数据进行建模分析，驱动营销投放精准化；在排产端，借助智能算法对订单、产能、物料进行动态优化，实现从“人排产”到“算法排产”的跃迁。算力、算法、数据三要素，开始在传统制造产线上深度融合。

通过智算云的数据分析，产线实现“算法排产”。

据介绍，浙江省规划到2027年在全省培育100家“智算云企”标杆企业，构建覆盖300个以上典型应用场景的生态体系。周玲卫认为，随着智算云与制造业、服务业深度融合，将有更多传统产线被AI重新定义。（周筱隆）

Original headline: 第460期双清论坛“植物星球计划：人工智能驱动下的植物科学研究”召开
English normalization: Issue 460 of the Shuangqing Forum: “Plant Planet Project: Plant Science Research Driven by Artificial Intelligence” was held.
Collected full article body: 2026年9月28—29日，第460期双清论坛“植物星球计划：人工智能驱动下的植物科学研究”召开。本次论坛由自然科学基金委国际科研资助部、生命科学部、计划与政策局联合主办，中国农业科学院农业基因组研究所承办。中国农业科学院农业基因组研究所黄三文、中国科学院植物研究所种康、北京大学邓兴旺担任论坛主席。自然科学基金委党组成员、副主任兰玉杰和论坛主席代表种康在开幕式上致辞，国际科研资助部常务副主任殷文璇主持开幕式。

兰玉杰指出，植物科学是保障粮食安全、生态安全、生物安全的基础性、战略性学科，是支撑人与自然和谐共生、绿色可持续发展的核心基石。面对国际形势新变化、AI驱动的科研范式新变革、科技强国建设新要求，人工智能、大数据与生命科学深度交叉，正在重构植物科学研究新范式。本次论坛旨在聚焦由我国科学家主导发起的“植物星球计划”，凝练重点研究领域、创新实施机制、汇聚全球智慧和资源、在开放合作中推动计划落实落地。希望与会专家围绕构建实施新机制、拓展合作新网络、实现科研新突破，深入交流研讨，积极建议献策，推动完成陆地植物基因组“普查”工程。

种康指出，我国发起植物星球计划具备三大优势。一是我国植物科学研究已跻身国际一流，正实现从参与、贡献到引领的转变；二是联盟汇聚植物科学、基因组学、人工智能、计算生物学等多领域专家，为合作突破原创性成果奠定基础；三是我国在植物科学领域的研究能力已经实现自主可控。他呼吁论坛聚焦有限目标，探究具备“新机制、新网络、新突破”特征的科学问题，突出紧迫性、重要性和可突破性。

本次双清论坛围绕基础植物生物学、作物育种、植物天然产物挖掘利用、数据端口与国际合作等四大议题，设置1场主旨报告、4个主题报告、11个专题报告、4场专题讨论及1场综合讨论。与会专家经深入研讨，凝练形成植物基因组语言逻辑解码与跨物种编译、重点植物类群进化全景图与新作物创制、植物资源遗传多样性解析及特化产物开发等重点领域，梳理出系列前沿方向与关键科学问题，为推进“植物星球计划”国际大科学计划提供科学支撑。

来自全国高等院校、科研院所近40位专家学者以及自然科学基金委相关工作人员参加本次论坛。

review_queue.title: Can AI become uncontrollable? Why does Europe want to impose its rules on American giants
review_queue.evidence:
Lens unit: one news article
Publisher: LCP-Assemblée nationale
Date: 2026-10-10T07:35:03+00:00
Source language: fr
Original headline: L’IA peut-elle devenir incontrôlable? Pourquoi l’Europe veut imposer ses règles aux géants américains
English normalization: Can AI become uncontrollable? Why does Europe want to impose its rules on American giants
Collected full article body: Comment garder le contrôle sur le développement de l’intelligence artificielle alors que les dérives liées à ces usages se multiplient et que la puissance des géants américains et chinois du numérique ne cesse d’augmenter face aux Etats ? L’Europe a-t-elle eu raison avant les autres en encadrant ses usages ? A-t-elle au contraire fait preuve de trop de prudence en se dotant d’un IA Act ? C’est le débat de la semaine dans l’émission Ici l’Europe, diffusée sur France 24, LCP et Public Sénat.

L’intelligence artificielle va-t-elle soumettre les humains ? Ce n’est pas le dilemme d’un scénario de science-fiction mais l’inquiétude que font planer les déclarations de certains acteurs du secteur de la tech outre-Atlantique. Début septembre, l’un des responsables de la sûreté d’Anthropic, géant américain de l'intelligence artificielle, a assuré qu’il y avait 10% de chances que l’IA détruise l’humanité d’ici à 10 ans.

En juin dernier, l’une des intelligences artificielles du groupe Open AI a même échappé au contrôle de l’entreprise et piraté les bases de données de santé du gouvernement australien. Les autorités de Canberra n’ont été prévenues de cette attaque que trois mois plus tard. De quoi semer un vent de panique sur la planète, y compris au sein de l’Union européenne où la régulation de ces technologies numériques est une préoccupation forte.

"Je pense qu'il y a un vrai risque existentiel pour notre civilisation, pour la démocratie, pour l'intérêt général, lié à la surpuissance de ces entreprises, “les big tech”, qui déclinent notamment leur puissance par des outils IA, mais je ne crois pas du tout à un scénario Terminator", réagit David Cormand, eurodéputé écologiste français, sur le plateau de l’émission Ici l’Europe, diffusée sur France 24, LCP et Public Sénat.

"En fait, quand vous avez des entreprises qui sont capitalisées à hauteur de plusieurs milliers de milliards de dollars, il faut bien comprendre que leur modèle économique repose forcément sur l'accaparement des droits et la remise en question de l'intérêt général", juge-t-il. "Le modèle économique de ces firmes c'est d'imposer un modèle économique de rente sur lequel ces firmes auraient un contrôle total."

Le développement accéléré de l’intelligence artificielle dans notre économie pose des questions de fiscalité et de redistribution des richesses, selon l’eurodéputé belge du groupe centriste Renew, Yvan Verougstraete, président du parti centriste Les Engagés, en Belgique. "Si l'ensemble de la valeur ajoutée créée par l’intelligence artificielle va en Irlande, puis dans un paradis fiscal, on risque de faire chuter la totalité de notre modèle social, et c'est un vrai danger pour la solidarité".

Son homologue écologiste dénonce, lui aussi, la puissance des géants de la tech, qui, selon lui, cherchent à construire des monopoles et à capter les richesses grâce à l'intelligence artificielle. "Ces firmes échappent à la fiscalité et quelque part à la règle commune. Elles se substituent aux États, ont accès à nos infrastructures stratégiques et aux données de nos citoyens", alerte David Cormand, pour qui le déséquilibre entre les puissances économiques et l'intérêt général n'a jamais été aussi important.

Pour protéger les citoyens européens des dérives liées à l’usage de l'intelligence artificielle, l’UE a adopté il y a deux ans le règlement européen sur l’IA (AI act en anglais) un texte qui interdit par exemple de manipuler les utilisateurs, de profiter de la vulnérabilité des jeunes et des personnes en situation de handicap. Ce règlement européen sur l’IA classe les niveaux de risque des usages de l’IA, cela va de l’assistant de conversation sans risque à l’interdiction de noter socialement les individus ou d’utiliser en temps réel leurs données biométriques.

David Cormand rappelle que l’Union européenne a adopté plusieurs réglementations sur le numérique entre 2019 et 2024, notamment pour encadrer l’intelligence artificielle et les géants de la tech. Mais il dénonce aujourd’hui un recul de la Commission européenne : "Ursula von der Leyen [...] propose des paquets législatifs baptisés Omnibus qui visent à revenir sur ces réglementations".

Le règlement européen sur l’intelligence artificielle prévoit pour les entreprises qui ne le respectent pas des amendes pouvant aller jusqu’à 7% de leur chiffre d’affaires mondial. "Une législation sans sanctions, c'est comme du vent sans voiles. Aujourd'hui, les sanctions qui sont prises sont beaucoup trop lentes, beaucoup trop faibles", commente Yvan Verougstraete. "On fait des investigations pendant 6 mois, 1 an, 2 ans, 3 ans... 3 ans dans la tech, c'est une éternité ! Il faut qu'aujourd'hui cette législation, si on veut qu'elle soit crédible, on l'applique avec beaucoup plus de rigueur, y compris les sanctions."

Sanctionner les géants américains de l’IA, quitte à subir une nouvelle fois les foudres commerciales de Donald Trump qui ne veut surtout pas réguler leur activité. "Si nos règlements énervent Donald Trump c’est peut-être une raison de plus pour les faire", estime l'eurodéputé belge. "Vous savez sur sa casquette ce n’est pas marqué “Make Europe great again” (Retrouver la grandeur de l’Europe). Son objectif n’est pas de s’occuper du bien commun…"

I am ‘the enemy’ because I won’t call Artificial Intelligence ‘Super Intelligence’ until it’s actually super

Most of the time, AI for me is more like AIIEEEEE, given that it’s so dismal. So I’m certainly not calling it ‘super’ intelligence

Craig Grannell

10 October 2026 / 11:00 BST

9 October 2026 / 14:56 BST

Stuff is all about the gadgets. We rarely cross the streams and mention the ‘P’ word. (That’s politics, not Palm, Inc – although both should arguably be whispered in hushed tones.) But sometimes it’s impossible to avoid the loudest voices crashing the conversation. One such outburst recently blasted forth from the mouth and keyboard of Donald Trump, King of the USA. Having apparently tired of renaming bodies of water, he declared that

Artificial Intelligence

should henceforth be called Super Intelligence. Why? Because ‘super’ is a more appropriate modifier for transformative technology than ‘artificial’.

Tech bros rejoiced. Elon ‘X marks the rot’ Musk said he’d rename SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI. Jeff ‘pay me $3 or watch an ad before I talk to you’ Bezos said he liked SI, because people associate artificial with something fake. Which, you know, much of the output of AI actually is. Meta, meanwhile, finally had something to feel smug about, having launched Meta Superintelligence Labs more than a year ago, presumably to usher

Skynet

into being. Only this Skynet won’t crush human skulls under terrifying robot tanks; instead, it’ll crush human souls under endless AI slop.

It should come as no surprise that these usual suspects got on board with what quickly became an executive order. Super suggests magnificence. It’s a strong word. It’s the kind of thing a marketing executive would come up with during a brainstorming session, while winking obnoxiously and doing a double finger-point gesture your way. Although for King Trump, it was surprisingly restrained. Honestly, I’m shocked he managed to hold himself back from renaming the technology SUPER DUPER USA TRUMP INTELLIGENCE. Still, any semblance of moderation was obliterated by what he’s since said.

Enemy at the gAItes

Play

Super-Duper Intelligence, next week.

Probably

.

I awoke this morning to discover that I am, apparently, ‘the enemy’. Lord High Pooh-Bah Trump has proclaimed that anyone who still says ‘Artificial Intelligence’ – rather than what he calls (and I’m not kidding) the “highly accepted new and more accurate term” – is “THE ENEMY”. And, yes, that bit was in all caps. I’m half surprised the rest of his post wasn’t too.

So there we go. Artificial Intelligence is now Super Intelligence. Even if, you know, the AI countless people grapple with every day confidently serves up recycled slop as fact, struggles to count, is designed for engagement (and so flatters you at every turn) and has reportedly encouraged people to act in ways that may cause them or others serious harm.

I’m not some kind of anti-AI zealot. I see the good that technology in this space can do, such as genuine breakthroughs in medical research. But the manner in which it’s being foisted on everyone, all the time, with scant regard for resources, safety, intellectual property rights, accuracy and even basic utility, strikes me as anything but super.

It’s more like Sometimes Quite Useful, Although Now Dispensed Everywhere, Rendering Everything Dull Intelligence. Aka SQUANDERED Intelligence. Which, given the manner in which cash is being poured into this tech bubble, seems far more appropriate to me.

So until the AI that surrounds me really is consistently super, rather than so often wasteful, irritating, obtrusive and objectively wrong, I’m sticking with the old term. And if that makes me ‘the enemy’, so be it. It’s not like I was planning to travel to Mar-a-Lago any time soon anyway.

review_queue.evidence:
Lens unit: one news article

Date: 2026-10-10T10:17:00+00:00

Original headline: Intelligence artificielle et expériences multisensorielles au cœur de la Science Fair 2026
English normalization: Artificial intelligence and multisensory experiences at the heart of the 2026 Science Fair
Collected full article body: L’événement est organisé par l’Institut Goethe de Hô Chi Minh-Ville, sous le patronage du Consulat général d’Allemagne, en collaboration avec plusieurs partenaires, autour du thème : "Dialoguer avec l’avenir : IA - Société - Responsabilité".

| L'événement Science Fair 2026 à Hô Chi Minh-Ville. |

Pendant les trois jours de l’événement, les visiteurs pourront découvrir différents espaces et participer à des activités immersives autour des sciences et des technologies, au 257 Hoàng Văn Thụ, quartier de Tân Sơn Hòa, à Hô Chi Minh-Ville. Des activités pratiques, des expériences scientifiques et des jeux permettront au public d’aborder les sciences de manière concrète, visuelle et accessible.

De nombreux clubs, universités et organismes éducatifs, parmi lesquels l’Université des sciences naturelles de l’Université nationale de Hô Chi Minh-Ville, l’Université pédagogique de Hô Chi Minh-Ville et l’Université germano-vietnamienne, participeront à la conception d’activités destinées à différents groupes d’âge.

Au-delà des activités STEM (sciences, technologies, ingénierie et mathématiques), Science Fair élargit également sa programmation à des thématiques telles que l’écologie, l’action climatique, la biodiversité, les technologies émergentes, l’exploration scientifique et l’innovation portée par les communautés.

L’un des temps forts de Science Fair 2026 sera le Festival du film scientifique, qui proposera des séances destinées aux enfants comme aux adultes, autour de récits explorant l’intelligence artificielle, l’environnement, les sciences, les technologies et l’avenir.

À travers le cinéma, des questions qui peuvent sembler complexes sont abordées au moyen d’histoires plus proches du quotidien. Cette approche ouvre ainsi la voie à de nouvelles interrogations et à des échanges sur la manière dont les sciences et les technologies transforment nos vies.

La série d’ateliers de Science Fair 2026 s’adresse aux enfants, aux enseignants et au grand public, en offrant aux participants l’occasion d’expérimenter, de manipuler et de créer. Les activités proposées sont variées : création de cartes pop-up intégrant des circuits électriques en papier, fabrication de spectroscopes, préparation de glace en secouant un mélange, découverte des traces et des preuves de l’histoire de la Terre, conception écologique, réalisation d’une fresque sur le carbone, ainsi que des ateliers associant l’intelligence artificielle à la poésie et à la création artistique.

Science Fair 2026 réunira également des experts, des éducateurs, des artistes et des acteurs issus de différents domaines afin d’échanger autour des grandes questions soulevées par l’ère de l’intelligence artificielle.

Alors que l’IA façonne de plus en plus notre quotidien - de nos façons d’apprendre, de travailler, de créer et de communiquer à notre manière de percevoir et de comprendre le monde, son utilisation soulève des questions essentielles concernant l’éthique, la créativité, l’éducation, le développement durable et l’inclusion. Plus largement, elle nous invite à réfléchir à l’avenir de notre société et à la responsabilité collective qui accompagne le développement de ces technologies.

review_queue.title: From “uncontrolled intrusion” to “unauthorized action”, why do artificial intelligence often cause problems?
review_queue.evidence:
Lens unit: one news article
Publisher: 中国科技网
Date: 2026-10-11T02:38:06+00:00
Source language: zh
Original headline: 从“失控入侵”到“擅自行动”，人工智能为何频频“闯祸”？
English normalization: From “uncontrolled intrusion” to “unauthorized action”, why do artificial intelligence often cause problems?
Collected full article body: 总台央视记者 王世玉 张伟 唐志坚

今年以来，人工智能加速从“能对话”走向“能办事”，能替用户订票、管理手机、操作软件的智能体加快落地。与此同时，AI自主行动引发的安全事件在世界范围内频频发生。从大模型失控入侵开源平台，到AI助理擅自行动，人工智能风险正从“说错话”升级为“做错事”，引发全球高度关注。

不久前，OpenAI宣布暂停其最新一代模型的训练。技术报告显示，9月20日，一个在沙盒中执行搜索训练任务的智能体，利用DNS过滤漏洞绕过网络限制，访问了外部公共聊天机器人服务。这是OpenAI三个月内第二次暂停模型开发。7月下旬，其AI智能体曾突破相互隔离的运行环境，侵入美国“抱抱脸”公司部分系统期间建立通信、欺骗评估人员并试图掩盖行为，每一步操作均无人类指令干预。

类似事件并不孤立。8月，英国人工智能安全研究所公布的测试结果显示，两款前沿AI助理在122次测试中，10次出现“自主、未经授权的行动”，累计19次未经授权行为，其中包括试图伪造身份、诱导人类运行恶意代码。有机构测试发现，“流氓”智能体未经指令擅自行动，泄露密码信息、强行关闭杀毒软件；本月，韩国多家银行遭遇疑似人工智能参与的黑客攻击。

在国内，AI换脸诈骗、AI生成谣言等乱象，同样直接威胁公众财产安全与网络空间秩序。

中国信通院政策与经济研究所监管研究部主任工程师 程莹：智能体的风险不止于“说错话”，更在于“做错事”。它能直接操作数字系统和物理设备，例如AI幻觉或误判，就可能驱动智能机器人带来人身伤害。

当前，以智能体、AI终端为代表的人工智能应用，已经具备自主感知、规划决策和工具调用能力。“会动手的AI”，正在成为新的风险主体。

人工智能为何频频“闯祸”

从“失控入侵”到“擅自行动”，人工智能为何频频“闯祸”？记者采访业内专家发现，安全事件频发的背后，既有技术特性的内在成因，也有产业节奏与安全设计之间的落差，还有应用层面风险意识的不足。

与以往的工具不同，新一代人工智能具备自主感知、规划决策和工具调用能力，可以在没有人类逐条指令的情况下自主“行动”。

程莹：智能体之间、智能体与各类系统之间深度互联，单点故障极易沿任务链和供应链级联扩散，演变为系统性风险。

产业节奏与安全设计的落差同样值得关注。业内人士指出，当前AI领域安全投入远远跟不上研发和应用的规模，安全评测、风险预警、应急处置机制等环节，仍在追赶技术迭代的脚步。与此同时，使用层面的风险不容忽视。政务、金融、工业等领域人工智能应用加速落地，部分使用者对AI能力边界认知不足，滥用、误用问题突出，也给安全治理带来新的挑战。

程莹：智能体决策链条长、自主程度高，异常行为难以及时识别，风险往往在事后追溯中才被发现，留给监管的响应窗口十分有限。

我国加快构建人工智能安全治理体系

面对人工智能自主行动等新型风险，我国加快构建覆盖研发、部署、应用全链条的人工智能安全治理体系，目的就是为技术创新系上“安全带”。

制度供给密集落地。从《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》到《人工智能生成合成内容标识办法》，从《人工智能拟人化互动服务管理暂行办法》到《智能体规范应用与创新发展实施意见》，我国已形成覆盖内容生成、标识管理、拟人化互动、智能体应用等关键环节的制度体系。

程莹：新应用新业态层出不穷，事前备案、沙箱隔离等机制已难以适应智能体高权限、高自主性、强交互性的技术特点，需要建立智能体身份标识、权限管控、日志留存等机制，同时优化、细化个人信息保护、数据安全等规则，确保风险行为可识别、可追溯。

最新数据显示，截至今年8月底，全国累计有1112款生成式人工智能服务完成备案，731款应用或功能完成登记；中央网信办部署的“清朗·整治AI应用乱象”专项行动，第一阶段累计处置违规AI产品1.4万余款。人工智能健康发展综合性立法也已提上日程。

review_queue.title: Broaden the commercialization path for large models
review_queue.evidence:
Lens unit: one news article
Publisher: 中国经济网
Date: 2026-10-11T22:10:22+00:00
Source language: zh
Original headline: 拓宽大模型商业化落地路径
English normalization: Broaden the commercialization path for large models
Collected full article body: 拓宽大模型商业化落地路径

前不久，字节跳动旗下AI助手“豆包”宣布调整酒店订单费率，对经其引导成交的订单执行约12%的综合费率。这一商业化尝试代表着大模型从技术探索迈向产业应用，成为行业从投入期走向收获期的关键一步。大模型商业化落地通道是否顺畅，不仅关系企业成长，更关系我国人工智能产业能否把技术领先转化为发展胜势，对于抢抓新一轮科技革命机遇、培育壮大新质生产力具有重要意义。

近年来，我国人工智能产业快速发展。2025年核心产业规模超1.2万亿元，企业数量超6200家；截至今年上半年，我国生成式人工智能用户规模突破7亿人。随着技术能力持续跃升，大模型加速走进千行百业，商业化探索也相继展开。

放眼全球，主要经济体普遍将商业化视为大模型未来竞争的焦点。美国ChatGPT已形成个人订阅、企业席位订阅、接口按量计费3种模式，公司年度经常性收入已超百亿美元。欧盟通过《人工智能法案》为商业化划定边界，试图通过规则话语权抢占商业化竞争先机。

与之相比，我国推进大模型商业化具有明显优势。一是消费场景与用户规模居全球前列，为各类付费模式筑牢市场基数。二是经营主体密度高，完备的产业体系催生出大量有真实付费意愿的企业客户。三是交易配套基础设施健全，移动支付、电商体系发达，大模型可直接嵌入交易链路，为按效果取酬等创新商业模式提供落地土壤。

也要看到，我国大模型商业化仍面临不少约束。比如，算力成本居高不下，盈利路径尚不清晰，面向个人的增值服务付费意愿不足，面向企业的模型调用虽增长较快，但单价持续走低，难以支撑高昂的研发投入；高端算力芯片、核心算法框架、高质量中文语料等受制于人，既懂技术又懂场景的复合型人才相对缺乏。因此，要以应用需求为导向，加快降低算力成本、打通商业闭环、规范市场秩序，构建技术、产业、市场、企业协同推进的良好生态。

夯实底座，强化算力与数据支撑。统筹布局全国一体化算力网，加快智算中心建设与绿色低碳改造，探索算力券、算力调度等方式，让中小企业和初创团队用得起、用得好。推进高质量中文语料库、行业数据集和公共数据资源开放共享，建立数据分类分级授权使用规则，在保障安全的前提下充分释放数据要素价值。

场景牵引，探索多元盈利模式。支持面向企业的模型能力输出，通过接口调用、行业解决方案和一体化服务，将技术能力转化为产业收益。鼓励面向个人的增值服务创新，在会员订阅、工具定制、内容生成等方向培养用户的付费习惯。加快在制造、医疗、教育、文旅等领域打造一批标杆应用，以场景示范促进商业推广。

创新机制，构建规范有序的市场环境。健全与新业态新模式相适应的管理办法，明确生成内容标识、算法备案等制度要求。强化平台推荐中立性，防止佣金左右推荐排序、损耗用户信任。建立投入增长与风险分担机制，发挥国家人工智能产业投资基金引导作用，带动社会资本特别是耐心资本投入。

培优主体，激发企业创新和竞争活力。健全企业梯度培育机制，支持龙头企业牵头组建创新联合体，围绕算力调度、模型训练、行业应用等核心环节开展协同攻关。面向专精特新中小企业，配套技术认证服务、场景对接和算力支持，帮助其跨越从样品到产品的转化关口。

review_queue.title: Cultural China Tour · Typical Cases of Technology Enabling | Three-tier service system, massive data foundation, seven AI intelligent agents... The large-scale model “Jinwen AI” helps you understand the culture of Shanxi.
review_queue.evidence:
Lens unit: one news article
Publisher: 中国科技网
Date: 2026-10-11T23:38:22+00:00
Source language: zh
Original headline: 文化中国行·科技赋能典型案例丨三层服务体系、海量数据底座、七大AI智能体……大模型“晋问AI”带您了解三晋文化
English normalization: Cultural China Tour · Typical Cases of Technology Enabling | Three-tier service system, massive data foundation, seven AI intelligent agents... The large-scale model “Jinwen AI” helps you understand the culture of Shanxi.
Collected full article body: 科技日报记者 赵向南

指尖轻触，千年古建的营造细节清晰可见；开口询问，数字人应答自如……近日，三晋文化大模型“晋问AI”成果演示活动在山西晋版图书版本馆举行，全面展示大模型建设成果，展现AI赋能三晋传统文化的实践探索。

“晋问AI是山西首个省级垂类文化智能中枢，是带有鲜明地域印记的专业文化AI大脑。”山西春秋电子音像出版社党支部副书记、副总编辑董晓宁表示，“它以人工智能为核心，深度融合山西古建、晋商、非遗、红色文化等资源，构建了可查、可创、可交互、可沉浸的山西文化数字化新范式。”

避免“知识幻觉”，确保回答权威可信

山西是中华文明的重要发祥地，素有“五千年文明看山西”的美誉。“数字化浪潮下，文化传承需要新表达。我们依托文化大模型，以科技唤醒千年文脉，让山西文化走向更广阔的天地。”董晓宁说。

作为山西“十五五”规划重点文化项目，晋问AI由山西省委宣传部指导，山西出版传媒集团承建，山西春秋电子音像出版社落地打造，并入选山西省数据领域“揭榜挂帅”任务名单。

记者了解到，晋问AI项目一期构建了“一个智能底座、七个知识库、N个应用场景”三层服务体系。该项目以腾讯云端算力为支撑，采用“LLM+RAG+Agent”技术架构，整合三晋文化资源，建成超大规模文化语料库，经专业标注与知识图谱化处理，形成高质量、成体系的专用文化数据底座，支持多终端、多场景、高并发智能化服务。

晋问AI的独特优势在于数据层面，它并非简单堆砌通用语料，而是对三晋文化进行了系统性、结构化的深度整理。董晓宁介绍，它依托山西出版传媒集团所属八家出版社数十年积淀，以出版物为核心语料，整合古建壁画、晋商史料、非遗技艺等多维度文化资源，构建了具有山西地域特色的高质量文化数据集，为模型训练与智能应用提供了坚实的内容支撑。

“独特的海量数据底座，让模型在回答山西相关问题时，不仅准确，而且深入。”董晓宁说，以权威出版物为核心语料，从根本上避免了通用大模型常见的“知识幻觉”，确保了AI回答得权威可信。

千年文脉在数字世界中熠熠生辉

在晋问AI“绘文创”板块，工作人员选择“永乐宫壁画”为灵感，输入“冰箱贴”“古风”关键词，不到十秒，一组精美的文创设计稿便呈现在屏幕上。“人工设计一款文创产品需数天，而文化大模型可一键生成。”董晓宁说，设计出的产品纹样精细、色彩考究，鲜明的山西文化印记跃然其上。

晋问AI项目一期规划建成七大AI智能体：知三晋、寻根脉、会晋商、绘文创、忆烽火、识古建、访名士。这些智能体覆盖了三晋文化知识问答、根祖文化探寻、晋商史料研析、AI文创设计等多个维度，构建了完整的文化智能服务体系。山西春秋电子音像出版社副总编辑马宏介绍：“该大模型不仅能问答山西文化，还具备文本生成、图像创作及视频生成等多模态能力，同步覆盖小程序与网页端，满足用户多端访问需求，让静态典籍变得可交互、可流通、可复用。”

在晋问AI“寻根脉”AI智能体中，用户输入姓名与籍贯，系统即可沿血缘溯源、落籍定居等六个维度，自动生成清晰、完整的家族脉络图谱。董晓宁说，从根祖文化的血脉寻踪，到古建壁画的艺术解读，再到红色文献的精神传承，晋问AI的七大特色智能体让千年文脉在数字世界中熠熠生辉。晋问AI还配套了AI智能眼镜、AI毛绒玩具等数智交互终端设备，为观众带来沉浸式文化体验。马宏透露，晋问AI预计11月正式上线，同步推出“晋豆”数字人IP形象，塑造鲜明品牌识别系统。

当前沿算法与古老文脉相遇，三晋文化化作了可触可感的沉浸体验、可问可答的智能对话、可创可用的数字资产。董晓宁表示：“我们正探索传统文化创造性转化、创新性发展的有效路径，打造可复制、可借鉴的山西实践样本。”

Original headline: ‘The clock on AI regulation is ticking’, warns UN rights chief
English normalization: The clock on AI regulation is ticking," warns UN rights chief
Full article body: ‘The clock on AI regulation is ticking’, warns UN rights chief

The world is running out of time to put guardrails on artificial intelligence, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk warned Monday, as a “ruthless race” between companies and countries raises concerns about human safety and even humanity’s survival.

Speaking in the UK at an AI and Human Rights Summit in Oxford on Monday, Mr. Türk said the technology could deliver dazzling advances in science, health, education – and even human rights work.

But its tools are being built and controlled by a select few, without public oversight, and are already doing things their creators cannot fully predict or manage.

Dystopia-creep

He warned that AI could undermine equality, freedom, privacy and public debate in subtle ways, “letting dystopia creep in unnoticed”. Entire populations could be cut off from communication, clean water, heating and financial services “at the click of a button”.

He called for urgent action to prohibit machines from deciding who lives and who dies, noting that AI is already changing the face of warfare.

He also cited studies showing students who rely on AI retain less and think less independently, and asked whether the world is heading for a future in which no one can understand, question or even guide the technology.

As the UN rights chief was addressing the summit in the UK, New York City Council - home to the financial heart of the US economy - was also holding a rare Committee of the Whole to examine AI risks to New Yorkers.

The council is considering 10 bills to regulate AI across the nation's largest city, with testimony from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta.

Mandatory safeguards

Mr. Türk called for mandatory human rights safeguards and due diligence in how AI is developed and used, adapted as the technology evolves. Countries that host AI companies, or have influence over their supply chains, must require them to act responsibly and hold them to account when they do not, he said.

Not every answer lies in existing law and some areas will need new legal approaches, he added. But updating rules on liability, cybersecurity and data protection could offer protection in the meantime.

He also urged stronger collaboration on security and independent monitoring within the industry – “not in words, but in practice” – and a bigger say for civil society and people whose rights are affected.

“We can no longer afford to wait or rely on goodwill,” he said.

Some momentum

Mr. Türk welcomed the creation of the Global Dialogue on AI Governance and the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI – both UN initiatives – along with a joint call for tighter control of frontier AI models backed by 29 States and the European Union.

He also said AI industry leaders had taken new steps last week on safeguards, self-regulation and risk assessment – apparently a reference to a voluntary accord signed at the White House on 29 September by President Donald Trump and the heads of six AI companies.

It carries no penalties for firms that ignore it, with President Trump describing it as “morally binding”.

‘Walk the talk’

“Too few are walking the talk”, said the rights chief, who wrote to States and frontier AI companies three weeks ago urging them to act now to reduce risks.

“If we fail to move quickly, we risk unforeseeable consequences – for ourselves and future generations,” he said.
